Add Google, iCloud, Nextcloud, Fastmail (via DAVx5) or Microsoft 365 / Exchange so their events show up here.

skb doesn\'t talk to Google, iCloud, Nextcloud, Fastmail or Microsoft 365 directly. Instead it reads whatever calendars Android already has — once you\'ve added an account through the helpers below, its events appear in the per-calendar list above.
DAVx5 is a free open-source app that adds CalDAV/CardDAV accounts to Android. After installing it, sign in once and your calendars will show up here.
Use Android\'s built-in Exchange account adder. If your phone doesn\'t ship Exchange, install Outlook or Nine Mail and sign in there instead.
If your accounts are already set up but not appearing, open Android\'s sync settings and confirm Calendar sync is enabled for each one.
Make skb your default calendar app?

Skb doesn\'t claim a system role — instead, the next time you tap a .ics file or calendar invite from another app, you\'ll see a chooser. Pick skb and tap \"Always\" to set the default. You can change this anytime from your phone\'s Settings.
Opens Android\'s default-apps screen so you can pick (or change) which app handles .ics files and calendar invites.
